product: USG FLEX, ATP and ZyWALL VPN
author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: For Zyxel ZLD firewalls (USG FLEX, ATP, ZyWALL VPN and USG); USG FLEX H runs uOS, whose output isn't documented. Add the data collector under Log & Report > Log Settings as a remote server in either format, VRPT/Syslog (the default, key="value") or CEF/Syslog, turn on the Security Policy Control and Traffic Log categories, and set the policies to log. The parent reads both formats into the same fields. Security policy decisions (msg "priority:<rule>, from <zone> to <zone>, <protocol>, service <service>, <action>" with note ACCESS BLOCK or ACCESS FORWARD) and other policy drops go to Netflow as blocked or allowed, with the rule, zones, service, note and user in event_metadata. Traffic logs go to Netflow as allowed, with the bytes each way, source NAT, the protocol number, application, client MAC, interfaces and duration. Other categories, such as IKE, interface statistics and the security services (IPS, anti-malware, sandboxing, content and URL filtering, IP reputation), stay generic with the device and time: Zyxel names the categories but publishes no message text for them. The time has no zone and is read as UTC; the year ZLD can add after it is read. How sure this is: Zyxel's ZLD CLI Reference and web help define the two formats, the CEF header and the record fields (time, msg, src, dst, note, pri, cat), and the ZLD handbook shows ACCESS BLOCK and ACCESS FORWARD. The line layout and the policy, traffic, IKE and interface statistics messages come from lines posted on Zyxel's community forum, in threads Zyxel staff answered (one says the Abnormal TCP drop is a Security Policy Control log). The allow wording in a policy msg and a CEF traffic log's extra keys are inferred from the VRPT lines; when msg's last word isn't a known action, the note decides. IPv6 addresses aren't documented and aren't handled. Samples are made up in those shapes. The child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (78 of 78 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. The child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (69 of 69 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). No built-in parser claimed these lines. The key="value" pairs are read with CEF(): in Run Test on 2026-10-16, Sophos NG-SIEM's SPLIT_NAME_VALUES cut a quoted msg that holds " key=" text into several fields, and with CEF() it stayed whole and all 81 fields matched the emulator.
